recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No core FHIR follow-up is recommended for FHIR-5621; any future reconsideration should be filed against the later Bundle.meta.security or extension-policy decisions rather than the original DSTU1 Coding-to-code change.
issue_request: FHIR-5621 was a Published Structured Documents DSTU1 change request asking why Composition.confidentiality was Coding rather than CodeableConcept. SDWG accepted a modified resolution to make the element a primitive code and provide a clinical document extension for alternate confidentiality coding systems.
initial_application: SVN revision 4660, imported as git commit 90a18571ed32b65db8e46fe83cb470e5347810ac, explicitly applied '#5621 - narrow confidentiality to a code' by changing the Composition spreadsheet type from Coding to code and updating examples to primitive confidentiality values.
additional_context: FHIR-17301 was later Published for R5 with a resolution to remove Composition.confidentiality and record Clinical Document confidentiality on the document Bundle's meta.security. Current core source reflects that later state: Composition is active, fhir.ini records Composition.confidentiality as removed, the StructureDefinition and search parameters no longer define it, the CDA note maps ClinicalDocument.confidentialityCode to Bundle.meta.security, and document examples use Bundle.meta.security. FHIR-37719 then deleted the otherConfidentiality extension because that content also belongs in Composition.meta.security or Bundle.meta.security; the Extension Pack now retains the old extension only as retired/deprecated with the reason 'Use Bundle.meta.security instead.'
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. Reintroducing or changing Composition.confidentiality, or reviving the alternate-code extension in core, would contradict the later Published R5 decisions and the current source state.
